help: read turns the file input into JSON rows; write turns the rows input into a new XLSX or CSV file.
Read boundary. Empty uses the application directory; relative input paths start here and resolved files must stay inside.
Worksheet name (exact, case-sensitive). Read: selects this worksheet; empty uses sheet_index. Write: names the created worksheet; empty uses Sheet1.
Worksheet position (1 = first) used when sheet is empty. Chart sheets are not counted.
Row holding the column names; rows above it are skipped. 0 means no header: rows are emitted as arrays.
Output format. Reading detects the format from the file extension (.xlsx, .xlsm, .csv, .tsv, .txt).
Existing destination directory. Empty uses this node's persistent storage (spreadsheets folder). Relative paths start at the application directory.
File name; the format extension is added. Placeholders: {date} and {time} (UTC), {unique} (random).
Replace an existing regular file with the same name. Off: an existing name fails and nothing is replaced.
Column order, e.g. ["id","name"]. Other keys are left out and reported. Empty keeps the order in which keys first appear.
Write the column names as the first row.
fail stops this node with an error. route publishes a content-free error document on the error port instead.
Leave out rows without any value; they are counted in the report.
When max_rows or max_columns is exceeded: fail, or keep the first rows/columns and flag the truncation in the report.
Accept .xlsm or macro-carrying workbooks. Macros are never run or kept; only cell values are read.
CSV only. escape prefixes text starting with = + - @ tab or carriage return with an apostrophe; reject fails; off writes it unchanged.
CSV field separator for reading and writing. It is never guessed.
CSV text encoding. utf-8-sig accepts an optional BOM when reading and writes one, as spreadsheet software expects.
Maximum data rows read, or rows written.
Maximum columns per row.
Maximum size in bytes of the source file, the rows input and the generated file.
Deadline for one operation, in seconds. Opening a workbook is not interruptible.
